newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Defaults reported in Vietnam as coffee prices soar.
newsitem.headline: Defaults reported in Vietnam as coffee prices soar.

text.p: Vietnamese robusta coffee prices have risen sharply this week amid volatility on world markets, but traders said on Friday the temptation for exporters to default in the current situation was becoming too great.
With only around 10,000 tonnes of coffee left in Vietnam from the 1996/97 crop there was little activity on the local or export markets.
FOB Saigon Port prices for Vietnamese robusta were quoted at around $2,300 per tonne compared to about $1,800 a week ago.
"There's coffee out here," said a trader in the main producing area of Dak Lak, "but there's not much of it and what is here is pretty poor quality."
Traders said, however, that the past week had seen the appearance of complaints about defaults by exporters on grounds they were unable to meet quality specification.
"That's their excuse, although obviously part of it is the price," one dealer said. "Now the rewards for defaulting are too big. The temptation is just too big."

A spectacular rally in coffee futures in New York continued for a third day on Thursday bringing July arabica prices to a life-of contract high of 318.00 cents, the highest price in two decades, before closing at 314.8 cents.
Traders in Vietnam said the London market was expected to open on Friday about $40 up on its Thursday close.
"But it's a wild market," said one. "So it's pretty hard to predict. As for New York -- it's just crazy."
